title: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: A World Foundation Model for Embodied Synthesis
hook: Instead of training a robot on real footage, generate the footage: a 38B image/video model that beats GPT-Image-2.0 at imagining robot scenes — and nearly doubles a real policy's success rate.
key_points: 38B-parameter model unifying text-to-image, image editing, embodied scene generation, transfer, and video generation in one framework.
Beats GPT-Image-2.0 in human evals on embodied scene generation/transfer; ranks #1 on World Arena for embodied video generation.
As a synthetic data engine, it lifts pi_0.5's real-world manipulation out-of-distribution success rate from 36.9% to 63.2%.
First model with high-quality multi-view scene generation across robot embodiments, plus controllable embodied transfer preserving consistency and dynamics.
Shows one foundation world model can serve as both an embodied simulator and a scalable data engine for training robot policies.
content_html: Most "foundation model for robotics" efforts fine-tune an image or video generator on scarce robot footage, and end up trading away the broad visual knowledge that made the base model good in the first place. Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 takes the opposite approach: a 38-billion-parameter multimodal autoregressive model that treats embodied generation — multi-view scenes, robot-state edits, action-conditioned video — as just another task alongside ordinary text-to-image generation and image editing, all trained jointly.
extra_html: Because embodied synthesis shares a backbone with general image/video generation, the model keeps the multi-view consistency, geometric coherence, and controllability that foundation generators have but robotics-specific models usually lack. It's the first model to generate high-quality multi-view scenes across multiple robot embodiments and to support "embodied transfer" — fine-grained edits to a scene that preserve consistency and interaction dynamics rather than just repainting pixels. In human evaluations it beats GPT-Image-2.0 on embodied scene generation and transfer, and tops the World Arena leaderboard for embodied video generation. The more consequential result: used generatively as a data engine, it boosted an existing manipulation policy (pi_0.5) from 36.9% to 63.2% out-of-distribution success on hard real-world tasks — evidence that a good enough world model can manufacture the training data a robot needs, not just simulate it. Xinghang Li and coauthors (Xiaomi Robotics), arXiv 2026; code and checkpoints at robotics.xiaomi.com.

related.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
related.hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.

related.title: World Action Models: A Survey
related.hook: Robots are learning to imagine the future before acting. This survey untangles 'world action models' from video generators and VLA policies — and finds them converging on one idea.

flashcards.prompt: Why does Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 treat embodied generation as an extension of foundation image/video generation, rather than training a separate robotics model?
flashcards.back_html: So it keeps the broad visual generalization learned from large-scale image/video pretraining instead of sacrificing it to adapt on limited robot data — the usual trade-off prior methods made.

flashcards.prompt: How is Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 actually used to improve a real robot policy's performance?

choices.text: As a data engine generating synthetic scenes/video to train and augment the policy
It directly replaces the policy's action head
It fine-tunes the policy's language encoder only
It only evaluates the policy, without generating training data

flashcards.explanation_html: Used generatively as a synthetic data engine, it lifted pi_0.5's real-world manipulation OOD success rate from 36.9% to 63.2%.

flashcards.prompt: What real-world manipulation result did pi_0.5 achieve after training with Xiaomi-Robotics-U0-generated data?
flashcards.back_html: Its out-of-distribution success rate on challenging real-world manipulation tasks rose from 36.9% to 63.2%.
